title: The House That Was Waiting
summary: At Hushwater, Maela Crow recognizes Kael as Darrow Keene and produces a sealed packet she has been holding for Darrow. Because Veyra and Samuel have remained with the group since the Long Mile, neither could have primed Hushwater during the current approach; the older provenance still has to be established.

panelPlan.text: Hushwater is a modest settlement of shaded houses and a communal dining court, with no obvious Sunforge in the immediate center.
Maela sees Kael, says 'Darrow Keene' with tired relief rather than shock, and goes inside before he can correct her.
Maela returns with a visibly old sealed cloth packet marked for DARROW KEENE. Its age proves only that Darrow's story predates the group; it does not yet prove when anyone connected Kael to Darrow.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: No, ma'am. My name is Kael Mack.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: Who told you he was coming?

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: No. And before you ask, she did not look like you.

directionInline.text: Do not use the packet's age as the causal proof. The packet establishes a real preexisting Darrow story. The dated household record of the later traveler, examined on Page 3, is what places the Kael-specific prediction before Veyra's operation.

title: The Promise in the Packet
summary: Maela explains that a dying friend asked her to hold the packet for Darrow Keene and that a later traveler described Kael's appearance closely enough that she believed the promise finally had an endpoint.

panelPlan.text: Maela sets the packet between herself and Kael but does not force it into his hands.
She explains that her friend Lysa died believing Darrow would come. Months later another traveler gave a description matching Kael.
Kael refuses to open the packet because it is addressed to someone else, frustrating Maela without disrespecting her promise.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Lysa made me promise I'd give this to Darrow.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: The woman described your face, your coat, even that thing you do when you want to leave.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: You stand half a step farther from everybody.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Because it says Darrow Keene. Looking like him doesn't make his mail mine.

directionInline.text: Keep the packet human and morally specific, not a glowing mystery artifact. Its contents do not need to be revealed to prove the larger causal problem.

title: Before Veyra
summary: Veyra reconstructs the dates from Maela's household ledger. The ledger records the later traveler who described a man matching Kael and linked him to Darrow; that visit predates Veyra first learning Kael's name and predates Samuel joining her. The explanation exposed in Issue 4 cannot have caused this setup.

panelPlan.text: Veyra lays her own dated notes beside Maela's household ledger. The relevant entry records the winter visitor, the Darrow name and enough of the description to show that the Kael-specific prediction existed before Veyra's case did.
Samuel asks for the traveler's description. Maela remembers a woman with a shaved left temple and a green scarf, nobody Samuel recognizes.
Eva watches Veyra try every ordinary explanation before finally accepting the chronology.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: This entry is five months before I first heard Kael's name.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: And I met Veyra after that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: So neither of you could have planted this one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Could the Varnok story have traveled backward somehow?

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You checked that date three times.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You only moved your finger three.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: I checked once before you came in.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: If it helps, I have been sick of this promise since winter.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: The traveler. Green scarf, shaved temple.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: If I had, I would have given her the packet and made it her problem.

directionInline.text: The causal proof is documentary chronology, not mystical certainty: Maela's ledger dates the Kael-like description and Darrow expectation before Veyra knew Kael's name. This falsifies Veyra/Samuel as the source of this particular setup while leaving ordinary unknown intermediaries possible.

title: We Know Him
summary: Eva and Jessa no longer reopen the possibility that Kael is secretly Darrow. Their months of ordinary life with him have made the identity question emotionally obsolete even while the external mystery deepens.

panelPlan.text: Outside Maela's house, Eva, Jessa, Veyra and Samuel argue over provenance while Kael sits apart mending a strap.
Veyra asks whether they can truly exclude Kael having some unknown connection to Darrow. Eva answers before Kael does.
Jessa backs her, not from theory but from accumulated knowledge of the person traveling with them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: We still have to consider that Kael knows more than he says.

dialogueInline.speaker: Veyra
dialogueInline.text: You cannot account for his whole life.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I don't need his whole life.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Of course they can. That is not the same as being a different person every time somebody wants one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: I believe the point is that Darrow is now the interesting part.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I preferred being the boring part.

directionInline.text: This is the character payoff: the audience is invited to stop treating Kael as a locked box. The mystery moves outward.

title: What the Promise Belongs To
summary: Kael helps Maela separate her promise to Lysa from the mistaken belief that he is Darrow. Maela decides to keep the packet rather than force closure through the wrong man.

panelPlan.text: Maela admits she wanted Kael to be Darrow because it would release her from carrying the promise.
Kael tells her he cannot release her, but that keeping a promise does not require pretending the wrong person fulfilled it.
Samuel watches Kael do pastoral work without naming it and understands why communities keep making use of him even when the assigned identity is false.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: I wanted you to be him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Then I could be finished with this.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: Lysa died believing he'd come. I promised her.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: So what am I supposed to do with it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: The preacher would have something better.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: I am trying very hard not to.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I only know I'm not Darrow. Opening it for me won't make your promise complete.

dialogueInline.speaker: Maela Crow
dialogueInline.text: So I still have to decide.

directionInline.text: Kael's humanity, not hidden identity, is what makes him useful. Samuel should recognize the contrast with his own manipulative use of people's needs.

title: The Question Moves
summary: The group leaves Hushwater with the first arc's human conspiracy definitively demoted from cause to interference. Eva states the new question: not who Kael is, but why people and stories keep arriving before him.

panelPlan.text: Maela remains at her doorway with the sealed packet, choosing not to manufacture closure.
The five travelers move out together; Veyra and Samuel are now plainly members of the moving group rather than agents positioned ahead and behind.
On the road, Eva closes the old page in her notebook labeled WHO IS KAEL? and starts a new one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: The page that says 'Who is Kael?'

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: That is a mildly alarming answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: The question is somewhere else now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Why do people keep getting a version of him before he gets there?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: I was hoping we'd stop having a question.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I still don't particularly need one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: What are you writing at the top?

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Best thing you've written all day.

directionInline.text: This is Worldview Reset #3. Veyra and Samuel are fellow witnesses now. Do not answer what lies behind the pattern; change the question cleanly.
